meaning: 權威公認的、符合正統的
example: This translation has become the canonical version studied in most universities.
roots: 同 canon 字源 + -ical (形容詞後綴) → 符合公認標準的

example: The politician's speech was full of moralistic cant but offered no concrete plan.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cantare (吟唱)，原指乞丐或宗教人士的吟誦腔調 → 引申為空洞虛偽的陳腔套話

example: The cantankerous old man complained about every small change in the neighborhood.
roots: 字源不確定，可能源自愛爾蘭語 cannran (抱怨) → 形容易怒好爭辯的性格

meaning: 遊說、逐戶拜訪徵求(意見、選票)
example: Volunteers canvassed the neighborhood, asking residents about the upcoming ballot measure.
roots: 源自 canvas (帆布)，早期指用帆布篩選穀物 → 引申為仔細徵詢、篩選意見

example: The capacious trunk of the old sedan could fit an entire family's luggage.
roots: capac- (能容納，拉丁文 capax) + -ious (形容詞後綴) → 能容納大量事物的

example: After a lengthy siege, the garrison finally capitulated to the invading army.
roots: capit- (頭，拉丁文 caput) + -ulate (動詞後綴) → 原指依條款(逐條列出)投降，引申為屈服讓步

example: The company's strategy seemed to shift with every caprice of the new CEO.
roots: 源自義大利文 capriccio (突然的顫抖，可能源自 capra 山羊的跳躍) → 如山羊跳躍般難以預料

meaning: 反覆無常的、變幻莫測的
example: Mountain weather can be capricious, shifting from sunshine to snow within an hour.
roots: 同 caprice 字源 + -ous (形容詞後綴) → 情緒或行為變化無常的

meaning: 吹毛求疵的、愛挑毛病的
example: The captious critic found fault with even the most minor details of the production.
roots: capt- (抓住，拉丁文 capere) + -ious (形容詞後綴) → 抓住小錯不放的

example: The storyteller captivated the children with tales of dragons and distant kingdoms.
roots: capt- (抓住，拉丁文 capere) + -ivate (動詞後綴) → 抓住注意力，使著迷

example: The sailors caroused in the harbor tavern late into the night.
roots: 源自德文片語 gar aus (trinken)，意為「喝乾杯」 → 引申為縱情飲酒作樂

example: Ignoring the carping comments from online critics, she continued to write in her own style.
roots: carp (源自古諾斯語 karpa，誇耀、抱怨) + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 不斷挑剔抱怨的

example: The report castigated the agency for its slow response to the disaster.
roots: cast- (純淨，拉丁文 castus) + -igate (使...，源自 agere) → 原指使人純淨，引申為嚴厲糾正批評

meaning: 催化劑；(引申)促成變化的因素
example: The protest served as a catalyst for widespread political reform.
roots: cata- (向下、完全) + lys (鬆解，希臘文 lysis) → 加速反應、促成改變的物質或事件

example: Government subsidies helped catalyze the growth of the renewable energy industry.
roots: 同 catalyst 字源 + -yze (動詞後綴) → 引發或加速某個過程

example: The spokesperson issued a categorical denial of all the allegations.
roots: category (範疇，希臘文 kategoria) + -ical (形容詞後綴) → 毫無保留地歸於明確類別，引申為斬釘截鐵的

meaning: (興趣、品味)廣泛的、包羅萬象的
example: Her catholic taste in music ranges from baroque opera to underground hip-hop.
roots: cata- (完全) + holos (整體，希臘文) → 涵蓋一切、廣泛包容的

example: His caustic remarks during the meeting left several colleagues visibly offended.
roots: 源自希臘文 kaustikos (能燃燒的，kaiein 燃燒) → 化學上有腐蝕性，引申為言語尖酸刻薄

meaning: 滿不在乎的、輕率傲慢的
example: Investors were alarmed by the CEO's cavalier attitude toward the company's mounting debt.
roots: 源自拉丁文 caballarius (騎士，caballus 馬) → 原指騎士階級的傲慢氣派，引申為輕率隨便

example: The financial advisor recommended the investment, with the caveat that markets can be unpredictable.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cavere (小心、提防) → 事先提出的警告或但書

example: Rather than address the main proposal, he caviled over minor wording issues.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cavillari (嘲弄、詭辯) → 針對細節無理挑剔

example: The treaty required the empire to cede several border territories to its rival.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cedere (走、讓步) → 讓出、放棄所有權

example: The rescue team responded with remarkable celerity, reaching the scene within minutes.
roots: celer- (快，拉丁文 celer) + -ity (名詞後綴) → 行動迅速的特質

example: Her censorious tone made it clear she disapproved of every decision the committee had made.
roots: censor (監察官，拉丁文，負責評判道德風紀) + -ious (形容詞後綴) → 習慣嚴厲批評指責的

example: The board voted to censure the director for misusing company funds.
roots: 源自拉丁文 censura (評判，與 censor 同源) → 正式且嚴厲地批評

example: The film is more cerebral than most action movies, favoring dialogue over explosions.
roots: cerebr- (大腦，拉丁文 cerebrum) + -al (形容詞後綴) → 訴諸理智思考而非情感的

meaning: 確信、篤定(常指主觀上的堅信)
example: He spoke with a certitude that left no room for doubt, though he was later proven wrong.
roots: cert- (確定，拉丁文 certus) + -itude (名詞後綴) → 內心確定不疑的狀態

example: Both sides agreed to an immediate cessation of hostilities.
roots: cess- (停止，拉丁文 cedere 的過去分詞 cessum) + -ation (名詞後綴) → 活動或狀態的終止

example: The young executive chafed under the strict rules imposed by upper management.
roots: 源自古法文 chaufer (加熱，與 chauffeur 同源) → 摩擦生熱，引申為因摩擦而惱怒

meaning: 穀殼、無價值的東西(常見於 separate the wheat from the chaff)
example: Editors must learn to separate the wheat from the chaff when reviewing submissions.
roots: 源自古英文 ceaf (穀殼) → 脫穀後剩下的無用外殼，引申為無價值之物

example: To her chagrin, the meeting was cancelled just as she finished preparing her presentation.
roots: 源自法文 chagrin (悲傷、煩惱)，字源不確定 → 因失望或難堪而產生的懊惱

meaning: 變色龍；(引申)善變、易於變換立場的人
example: As a political chameleon, he shifted his positions to match whatever audience he addressed.
roots: 源自希臘文 khamaileon (地上的獅子，khamai 地面 + leon 獅子) → 因該蜥蜴能變色而引申為善變之人

example: Everyone in the office knew the polite handshake was just a charade masking deep resentment.
roots: 源自法文 charade (猜謎遊戲) → 引申為表面裝飾、實則虛假的行為

example: The self-proclaimed healer turned out to be a charlatan selling nothing but false hope.
roots: 源自義大利文 ciarlatano (吹噓叫賣的小販，ciarlare 喋喋不休) → 靠花言巧語行騙的人

example: Investors remained chary of the volatile market after last year's crash.
roots: 源自古英文 cearig (悲傷的、憂慮的，與 care 同源) → 因憂慮而格外謹慎

example: A growing chasm has emerged between the party's moderate and radical factions.
roots: 源自希臘文 khasma (裂口、深淵) → 引申為觀點或狀態上的巨大鴻溝

example: The chapel's chaste interior contrasted sharply with the ornate cathedral next door.
roots: 源自拉丁文 castus (純淨的、無瑕的) → 引申為純潔或樸素不加修飾的

example: The coach chastised the players for their careless mistakes during the match.
roots: 同 chaste 字源，原意為使純淨 → 引申為透過責罰使人改正

meaning: 沙文主義、盲目的偏執愛國(或性別)心態
example: His constant dismissal of his female colleagues' ideas reflected deep-seated chauvinism.
roots: 源自法國士兵 Nicolas Chauvin，因其對拿破崙的盲目崇拜而得名 → 引申為過度偏執的優越感

meaning: 沙文主義的、盲目偏執的
example: The film was criticized for its chauvinistic portrayal of women as mere sidekicks.
roots: 同 chauvinism 字源 + -istic (形容詞後綴) → 帶有盲目優越感的

meaning: (外貌)天真可愛的、如天使般的
example: The cherubic toddler charmed everyone at the family reunion with his round cheeks and giggles.
roots: cherub (源自希伯來文 kerub，天使) + -ic (形容詞後綴) → 具有天使般純真可愛外貌的

example: The merger was pushed through only through a series of legal chicanery.
roots: 源自法文 chicane (無理取鬧的爭執，可能源自波斯馬球術語) → 引申為狡猾欺詐的手段

example: The librarian gently chided the students for talking too loudly.
roots: 源自古英文 cidan (爭吵、責罵) → 以言語表達不滿或責備

meaning: 空想、不可能實現的幻想；(神話)喀邁拉獸
example: Critics dismissed the plan for a self-sustaining colony on Mars as a chimera.
roots: 源自希臘神話 Khimaira (獅頭、羊身、蛇尾的怪獸) → 引申為虛幻不切實際的想法

example: His chimerical scheme to double the company's revenue overnight convinced no one on the board.
roots: 同 chimera 字源 + -ical (形容詞後綴) → 如神話怪獸般虛幻不真實的

example: Guests were unimpressed by the chintzy decorations at the otherwise expensive wedding.
roots: 源自 chintz (印花棉布)，因廉價印花布在19世紀被視為俗氣 → 引申為廉價又小氣的

meaning: 有騎士風度的、彬彬有禮的
example: He held the door open and offered his seat, a chivalrous gesture that impressed everyone.
roots: chival- (騎士，源自古法文 chevalier，來自拉丁文 caballus 馬) + -rous (形容詞後綴) → 具有中世紀騎士般的禮節與勇氣

meaning: 騎士精神、彬彬有禮的風度
example: The novel romanticizes medieval chivalry, portraying knights as paragons of honor.
roots: 同 chivalrous 字源 → 騎士應具備的美德與禮儀

example: The choleric general was known for shouting at subordinates over the smallest mistake.
roots: choler (膽汁，希臘文 khole) + -ic (形容詞後綴) → 古代體液學說認為膽汁過多導致易怒

example: The documentary chronicles the rise and fall of the once-dominant newspaper industry.
roots: chron- (時間，希臘文 chronos) + -icle (名詞/動詞後綴) → 依時間順序記錄事件

example: It seemed churlish to refuse the invitation after they had gone to so much trouble.
roots: churl (源自古英文 ceorl，平民、粗人) + -ish (形容詞後綴) → 帶有粗俗無禮舉止的

example: Roadwork forced drivers to take a circuitous route through the back streets.
roots: circuit (源自拉丁文 circuitus，環繞) + -ous (形容詞後綴) → 繞遠路的、非直接的

meaning: 迂迴累贅的說法、拐彎抹角
example: Instead of a simple yes or no, the spokesperson offered pages of circumlocution.
roots: circum- (周圍) + loc (說，拉丁文 loqui) + -ution (名詞後綴) → 繞著主題說話而不直接表達

example: Magellan's crew was the first to circumnavigate the globe by sea.
roots: circum- (周圍) + navig (航行，拉丁文 navigare) + -ate (動詞後綴) → 繞著某物航行一周

example: The new law circumscribes the powers previously granted to local governments.
roots: circum- (周圍) + scribe (寫，拉丁文 scribere) → 在四周畫線界定範圍

meaning: 謹慎小心的、考慮周全的
example: Given the market's volatility, the fund manager took a more circumspect approach to investing.
roots: circum- (周圍) + spect (看，拉丁文 spicere) → 環顧四周後才行動，形容謹慎

example: The company restructured its operations abroad to circumvent the new tariffs.
roots: circum- (周圍) + vent (來，拉丁文 venire) → 繞道而行，避開正面阻礙

example: Despite their political disagreements, the two candidates debated with notable civility.
roots: civil (公民的、有禮貌的，拉丁文 civilis) + -ity (名詞後綴) → 符合社會禮儀的態度

meaning: 有洞察力的(人)、能預知的(人)
example: Her clairvoyant grasp of market trends made her one of the firm's most valuable analysts.
roots: clair- (清楚，法文 clair) + voyant (看見的，voir) → 能清楚看見常人看不見之事物

example: Public clamor for reform grew louder after the scandal was exposed.
roots: 源自拉丁文 clamare (喊叫) → 大聲呼喊、要求

example: The two rival companies held a clandestine meeting to discuss a potential merger.
roots: 源自拉丁文 clandestinus (秘密的，clam 秘密地) → 刻意隱藏不讓人知道的

example: The clannish group of veteran employees rarely welcomed new hires into their circle.
roots: clan (氏族，蘇格蘭蓋爾語 clann) + -ish (形容詞後綴) → 像氏族般緊密團結卻排斥外人的

meaning: 劈開、分裂；(反義)緊緊依附
example: The axe cleaved the log neatly in two with a single blow.
roots: 源自兩個不同的古英文詞根 cleofan (劈開) 與 clifian (黏附) 巧合合流 → 是英文中少見同形反義的「矛盾詞」

example: The governor granted clemency to the prisoner after new evidence emerged.
roots: clement (溫和的，拉丁文 clemens) + -cy (名詞後綴) → 對他人過錯展現寬容的態度

meaning: 溫和的、寬厚的(常指天氣或態度)
example: The unusually clement winter meant fewer heating costs for local residents.
roots: 源自拉丁文 clemens (溫和的、仁慈的) → 形容天氣或人態度溫和

example: The graduation speech was filled with clichés about following your dreams.
roots: 源自法文 cliché (印刷業術語，指鑄版)，因鑄版被重複使用而引申為被過度使用的表達方式

example: The popular clique at school rarely let anyone else sit at their lunch table.
roots: 源自法文 clique (小團體)，可能與擬聲詞 cliquer (發出喀噠聲) 有關 → 引申為排他的小群體

meaning: (議會)結束辯論、限制發言的程序
example: The Senate invoked cloture to end the filibuster and proceed to a final vote.
roots: 源自法文 clôture (關閉，與 close 同源) → 用以終結冗長辯論的正式程序

example: As the company's largest shareholder, she carried enormous clout on the board.
roots: 源自古英文 clut (一擊、補丁) → 原指用力一擊，引申為具有份量的影響力

meaning: 過分甜膩的、令人生厭的
example: The cloying sweetness of the dessert made it hard to finish more than a few bites.
roots: 源自 cloy (使厭膩，古法文 encloyer 釘死) + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 甜膩到令人反感的程度

example: The various protest groups gradually coalesced into a single unified movement.
roots: co- (一起) + alesce (成長，拉丁文 alescere) → 各部分成長合為一體

example: The two smaller parties formed a coalition to challenge the ruling majority.
roots: 同 coalesce 字源 + -tion (名詞後綴) → 各方結合而成的聯合體

example: It took nearly an hour to coax the frightened cat down from the tree.
roots: 源自中古英文俚語 cokes (愚人)，coax 原意為「愚弄」 → 引申為以溫和手段誘導對方順從

meaning: 自信滿滿的、過度自負的
example: The cocksure rookie assured everyone he'd win the tournament in his first attempt.
roots: cock (公雞，象徵自負) + sure (確定的) → 像公雞般昂首自信、過分篤定

meaning: (音樂或事件的)結尾部分、尾聲
example: The peace treaty served as a fitting coda to years of brutal conflict.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cauda (尾巴) → 附加在主體之後的結束部分

example: Critics argue the policy coddles large corporations at taxpayers' expense.
roots: 字源不確定，17世紀起指用溫水慢煮，引申為細心呵護 → 過度小心地照顧使其軟弱

example: The witness claimed she had been coerced into signing the false statement.
roots: co- (加強) + erce (限制，拉丁文 arcere) → 強行限制、逼迫對方行動

example: The confession was later ruled inadmissible because it had been obtained through coercion.
roots: 同 coerce 字源 + -ion (名詞後綴) → 用力量或威脅迫使他人服從

example: Human rights groups condemned the regime's coercive interrogation tactics.
roots: 同 coerce 字源 + -ive (形容詞後綴) → 帶有強迫性質的

example: The two philosophers, though coeval, never actually met in person.
roots: co- (共同) + aev (時代，拉丁文 aevum) + -al (形容詞後綴) → 存在於同一時期的

meaning: 有說服力的、令人信服的
example: She presented a cogent argument that swayed even the most skeptical board members.
roots: co- (一起) + gent (驅使，拉丁文 agere) → 把論點緊密地驅趕在一起，形成有力的論證

example: He spent the afternoon cogitating on the ethical implications of the new technology.
roots: co- (一起) + git (驅使，拉丁文 agitare 反覆推動) → 反覆推敲思考

example: "Night" in English and "Nacht" in German are cognate words derived from a common root.
roots: co- (共同) + gnate (出生，拉丁文 gnasci) → 出自同一根源的

example: The committee took cognizance of the new evidence before reaching its decision.
roots: cogn- (知道，拉丁文 cognoscere) + -izance (名詞後綴) → 對某事有所認識的狀態

example: Employees should be cognizant of the risks before signing the new contract.
roots: 同 cognizance 字源 → 對某事有清楚認識的

example: The tiny wine bar is known mostly to local cognoscenti rather than tourists.
roots: 源自義大利文 cognoscente (知曉者，與 cognizant 同源) → 對特定領域有深入了解的行家

meaning: 緊密結合的、有凝聚力的
example: The new coach quickly turned a group of individual stars into a cohesive team.
roots: co- (一起) + hes (黏著，拉丁文 haerere) + -ive (形容詞後綴) → 各部分緊密黏合在一起的

example: Researchers spent months collating data from hundreds of separate studies.
roots: col- (一起) + late (帶來，拉丁文 latus) → 把資料收集在一起加以比對整理

example: The airstrike caused significant collateral damage to nearby residential buildings.
roots: col- (一起) + later (側邊，拉丁文 latus) + -al (形容詞後綴) → 位於主體側邊、附帶伴隨的

example: The department prides itself on a collegial atmosphere where junior staff can freely challenge senior researchers.
roots: colleg- (同事，拉丁文 collega) + -ial (形容詞後綴) → 具有同僚間合作精神的

example: The professor's colloquial teaching style made even dense theory feel approachable.
roots: col- (一起) + loqu (說話，拉丁文 loqui) + -ial (形容詞後綴) → 日常交談中使用的語言風格

example: The two scholars engaged in a lengthy colloquy on the nature of consciousness.
roots: 同 colloquial 字源 → 雙方深入交流的正式對話

example: Regulators accused the two airlines of colluding to fix ticket prices.
roots: col- (一起) + lude (玩，拉丁文 ludere) → 私下一起玩弄手段，引申為共謀

example: The investigation found no evidence of collusion between the two companies.
roots: 同 collude 字源 + -ion (名詞後綴) → 秘密合謀的行為

example: Rebuilding the flooded city will require a colossal investment of both money and time.
roots: coloss- (巨像，希臘文 kolossos) + -al (形容詞後綴) → 如巨像般規模驚人的

meaning: 巨像、巨人般的人物或事物
example: The company grew from a garage startup into a colossus dominating the entire industry.
roots: 源自希臘文 kolossos (巨大雕像，如羅德島太陽神銅像) → 引申為體積或影響力極其龐大之物

meaning: 昏迷的；(引申)呆滯無生氣的
example: After the marathon, he collapsed onto the couch, practically comatose with exhaustion.
roots: coma (昏迷，希臘文 koma 深睡) + -tose (形容詞後綴) → 陷入深度無意識狀態的

meaning: 容貌姣好的、討人喜歡的
example: The old ballad describes a comely maiden who charmed every villager she met.
roots: 源自古英文 cymlic (合適的、美麗的) → 外表令人賞心悅目的

meaning: 禮讓、友好和睦的關係(尤指國家間)
example: The treaty was signed in a spirit of comity between the two long-time rivals.
roots: com- (共同) + ity (源自拉丁文 comitas，禮貌友善) → 彼此尊重和睦相處的關係

example: Her salary was hardly commensurate with the long hours and heavy responsibilities of the job.
roots: com- (共同) + mensurate (測量，拉丁文 mensurare) → 用同一標準衡量後相符的

example: In the old quarter, ancient traditions commingle freely with modern street art.
roots: com- (一起) + mingle (混合) → 使不同事物融合在一起

example: Coworkers gathered to commiserate with her over the sudden loss of her job.

meaning: 閃爍發光；(比喻，才華等)光彩四射
example: Her coruscating wit made her the most sought-after dinner guest in the city.
roots: 源自拉丁文 coruscare (閃爍、震動) → 引申為才智或言語如光芒般耀眼奪目

example: Growing up in five different countries gave her a truly cosmopolitan outlook on life.
roots: cosmo- (世界，希臘文 kosmos) + polit (城市、公民，希臘文 polis) + -an (形容詞後綴) → 視整個世界為自己家園的

example: The child had been so cosseted by his grandparents that he struggled with the discipline of school.
roots: 源自古英文 cot-sǣta (住小屋的人，引申為寵物羊) → 像對待寵物般精心呵護

meaning: 便秘的；(比喻)吝嗇的、遲鈍的
example: The negotiations stalled thanks to the delegation's costive approach to every concession.
roots: cost- (源自拉丁文 constipare，壓緊、擠壓) + -ive (形容詞後綴) → 原指身體阻塞，引申為態度上的吝於付出或遲滯不前

meaning: 小圈子、志同道合的一群人
example: The professor was surrounded by a small coterie of devoted graduate students.
roots: 源自古法文 coterie (佃農聯合租地的小團體) → 引申為緊密結合的小圈子

example: The principal refused to countenance any form of bullying on school grounds.
roots: counten- (源自拉丁文 continere，容納、克制) + -ance (名詞後綴) → 原指維持鎮定的表情，引申為表示認可

example: Regular exercise can help counteract the negative effects of a sedentary job.
roots: counter- (相反) + act (行動) → 採取行動抵銷相反力量

example: Customs officials confiscated thousands of counterfeit handbags at the border.
roots: counter- (相對應) + feit (做，拉丁文 facere) → 仿照原物做出來的假貨

meaning: 撤銷(命令)、發布相反命令
example: The general countermanded the earlier retreat order and pushed the troops forward.
roots: counter- (相反) + mand (命令，拉丁文 mandare) → 下達與原命令相反的指示

example: The court weighed the countervailing interests of free speech and public safety.
roots: counter- (相對) + vail (有價值，拉丁文 valere) + -ing (形容詞後綴) → 提供相反力量以達平衡的

example: The military seized power in a swift, bloodless coup.
roots: 源自法文 coup (打擊)，源自拉丁文 colpus → 一次突然而果斷的行動

meaning: 設法贏得(支持、青睞)；招致(危險)
example: By ignoring the safety warnings, the company was courting disaster.
roots: 源自拉丁文 cohors (庭院、隨從) → 原指在宮廷中討好君主，引申為刻意追求或招致某事

example: The two nations signed a covenant promising mutual defense in the event of invasion.
roots: 源自古法文 covenir (一致同意，拉丁文 convenire) → 雙方共同同意並承諾遵守的約定

example: The agency ran a covert operation to gather intelligence on the smuggling ring.
roots: 源自古法文 covert (被覆蓋的，couvrir 覆蓋) → 被遮蓋而不為人知的

meaning: 覬覦、渴望擁有(他人之物)
example: Rival studios coveted the streaming rights to the wildly popular series.
roots: 源自古法文 coveitier (強烈渴望)，源自拉丁文 cupere → 強烈渴望得到(通常屬於他人的東西)

example: He cast a covetous glance at his neighbor's newly renovated kitchen.
roots: 同 covet 字源 + -ous (形容詞後綴) → 帶有強烈貪求慾望的

example: The witness refused to be cowed by the defense attorney's aggressive questioning.
roots: 源自古諾斯語 kuga (壓迫、恐嚇) → 以威嚇手段使人退縮順從

example: The dog cowered in the corner every time the thunder rumbled overhead.
roots: 源自中古低地德文 kuren (蹲伏) → 因恐懼而蜷曲身體

meaning: 忸怩作態的、故作靦腆的
example: She remained coy about the details of her new project, hinting only that it was "big."
roots: 源自古法文 coi (安靜的，拉丁文 quietus) → 引申為故意保持含蓄、不直接表態

example: His crass jokes about the layoffs were met with stony silence from the room.
roots: 源自拉丁文 crassus (厚的、密的) → 引申為思想或言行粗鈍不敏感的

example: His craven refusal to defend his colleague in the meeting disappointed the entire team.
roots: 源自古法文 cravanter (壓垮、擊敗) → 被擊垮而顯得怯懦的

example: The committee gave little credence to the anonymous complaint without supporting evidence.
roots: cred- (相信，拉丁文 credere) + -ence (名詞後綴) → 對某事物予以相信的程度

example: The scam preyed on the credulity of elderly investors who trusted the friendly salesman.
roots: 同 credulous 字源 + -ity (名詞後綴) → 過於容易相信他人的傾向

example: Credulous readers shared the fabricated news story without checking its source.
roots: cred- (相信，拉丁文 credere) + -ulous (形容詞後綴) → 過於容易相信、缺乏懷疑的

example: Tolerance for differing opinions was a core creed of the small liberal college.
roots: 源自拉丁文 credo (我相信) → 個人或團體所堅信的原則

example: The protest built to a crescendo as thousands more demonstrators joined the march.
roots: 源自義大利文 crescendo (逐漸增強，crescere 成長) → 逐步增強直至頂點

example: The crestfallen team trudged off the field after losing the championship in overtime.
roots: crest (雞冠、鳥冠) + fallen (垂落的) → 如同鳥冠垂落般失去了原有的神氣

meaning: (尤指政商)老友、密友(常帶貶意)
example: The mayor was accused of awarding city contracts to his cronies instead of the lowest bidder.
roots: 源自17世紀劍橋大學俚語 chronios (同齡的，希臘文 chronos 時間) → 引申為長年結交、關係密切的朋友

example: Critics accused the administration of rampant cronyism in its hiring practices.
roots: 同 crony 字源 + -ism (名詞後綴，表主義、行為) → 憑私交而非能力任用親信的行為

example: The startup's first year became a crucible that tested every founder's resolve.
roots: 源自中古拉丁文 crucibulum (熔煉容器)，字源可能與 crux 十字架有關 → 高溫熔煉金屬的容器，引申為淬鍊性格的嚴峻環境

example: The crux of the dispute was not money but a fundamental disagreement over control of the company.
roots: 源自拉丁文 crux (十字架、難題) → 事情最關鍵、最難解的部分

example: The billionaire's cryptic tweet left investors guessing about the company's next move.
roots: crypt- (隱藏，希臘文 kryptos) + -ic (形容詞後綴) → 意義隱藏不明的

example: The editor culled the best essays from over a thousand submissions for the anthology.
roots: 源自拉丁文 colligere (聚集、挑選，與 collect 同源) → 從一大群中篩選出部分

meaning: 以...達到高潮、最終演變為
example: Years of research culminated in a breakthrough discovery published last month.
roots: culmin- (頂點，拉丁文 culmen) + -ate (動詞後綴) → 到達最高點、最終結果

example: The championship win was the culmination of a decade of hard training.
roots: 同 culminate 字源 + -ion (名詞後綴) → 發展到達的最終高點

example: The investigation found the contractor culpable for the building's structural failure.
roots: culp- (過錯，拉丁文 culpa) + -able (形容詞後綴) → 應為過錯負責的

meaning: 培養(能力、關係、興趣)；耕種
example: The mentorship program helps young employees cultivate leadership skills early in their careers.
roots: cult- (耕種，拉丁文 colere) + -ivate (動詞後綴) → 悉心栽培使其成長

example: The approval process is so cumbersome that most small projects never get past the paperwork.
roots: cumber (阻礙，源自古法文 combrer 堵塞) + -some (形容詞後綴) → 造成阻礙、難以操作的

example: The cunning fox managed to slip past the farmer's dogs undetected.
roots: 源自古英文 cunnan (知道、能夠) → 引申為運用智謀達成目的的

example: The scandal exposed the sheer cupidity of executives who looted the pension fund.
roots: cupid- (慾望，拉丁文 cupiditas，與愛神 Cupid 同源) + -ity (名詞後綴) → 對財富或利益的強烈貪求

example: The new regulations aim to curb excessive speculation in the housing market.
roots: 源自古法文 courbe (彎曲的，拉丁文 curvus) → 原指套在馬嘴上的彎曲鏈條，用以控制馬匹，引申為抑制行為

meaning: 脾氣暴躁的老人、易怒的人
example: The old curmudgeon next door yells at anyone who steps on his lawn.
roots: 字源不確定，16世紀出現，一說源自法文 coeur méchant (惡毒的心) → 引申為性情乖僻好抱怨的人

example: A cursory glance at the report was enough to spot several glaring errors.
roots: curs- (跑，拉丁文 currere) + -ory (形容詞後綴) → 匆匆跑過、未加細究的

example: His curt reply to her question made it clear he didn't want to discuss it further.
roots: 源自拉丁文 curtus (縮短的) → 話語簡短到近乎無禮

example: The airline was forced to curtail its flight schedule due to the fuel shortage.
roots: curt- (縮短，拉丁文 curtus) + -ail (動詞後綴，可能受 tail 尾巴影響) → 剪短、削減

example: The government's emergency fund helped cushion the economy against the worst effects of the recession.
roots: 源自古法文 coissin (坐墊) → 像坐墊般吸收緩解衝擊力

meaning: 憤世嫉俗者、懷疑他人動機的人
example: Even the biggest cynic in the office admitted the new policy was a genuine improvement.
roots: 源自希臘文 kynikos (犬儒學派，kyon 狗) → 犬儒學派主張輕視世俗價值，引申為對人性抱持懷疑態度的人

meaning: 憤世嫉俗的、懷疑他人動機的
example: Years of political scandal have left many voters deeply cynical about government promises.
roots: 同 cynic 字源 + -al (形容詞後綴) → 傾向懷疑他人真誠、看淡理想的

example: Her early idealism gradually gave way to cynicism after years of watching corruption go unpunished.
roots: 同 cynic 字源 + -ism (名詞後綴) → 對人性或世事抱持懷疑貶低態度的思想傾向

meaning: 眾所矚目的焦點、引導的中心
example: With her stunning gown, she quickly became the cynosure of the entire gala.
roots: 源自希臘文 kynosoura (小熊座，字面意為狗尾) → 古代航海者依此星座導航，引申為眾人目光的中心
